title: The shortcut pattern
drDigitalIntro:
Here is the secret: shortcuts follow one simple pattern.
• Hold Ctrl (or Command on a Mac) and press a letter.
• C copies, V pastes, X cuts, Z undoes, S saves.
• A selects all, B bolds, I italicizes, U underlines.
• The letter is always a clue: C = Copy, V = paste (the V points down like a pour), Z = undo (the last letter — last chance!).
• Once you know the pattern, you can guess most shortcuts without looking them up.

playgroundTask.goal: Practice the three most useful keyboard shortcuts

steps.say: Type a short sentence in the notes editor below.
Press Ctrl+A (or Command+A) to select everything you typed.
Press Ctrl+C (or Command+C) to copy the selected text.
Press Ctrl+Z (or Command+Z) to undo and bring back your text.

drDigitalSuccess: You have got the pattern — Ctrl (or Command) plus a letter. That unlocks almost every shortcut!
drDigitalHint: Try each shortcut in order. The glowing button in the toolbar shows you what to do next. Hold Ctrl and press the matching letter.
